title: Gabber local duality and finite field coefficients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $\delta$ be a dimension function and $K$ a pinned potential dualizing complex on $(X,\delta)$ [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Let $A$ be a finite field with a unital map $\Lambda\to A$, and put $K_A=A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then $K_A$ is bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the functor $D_A=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,K_A)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] preserves $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and for every $M$ in that category the evaluation-transpose map
$$M\longrightarrow D_AD_AM$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $M$. The normalization of $K_A$ is obtained by scalar extension of the pinnings of $K$. No bound on the cohomological dimension of the residue fields of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Theorem 6.1.1 and Theorem 7.1.3 (A a finite field, so bounded constructible complexes have finite Tor amplitude); Definition 7.1.1 for evaluation biduality

proof.text: Apply the prime-power form of Gabber's local duality theorem with $r=1$. At $r=1$, the definition of pinned potential complex in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex] is exactly the current [def-per-potential-dualizing]: residue-field pinnings are compared only after passage to geometric fibres; immediacy is measured in the strict localization; and the transition uses the residue degree after that localization. Thus the given $K$ satisfies the theorem's hypothesis. The Noetherian, excellence and invertibility assumptions are explicitly present. The theorem gives bounded constructibility of $K$, preservation of $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ by $D_K$, and its natural evaluation-transpose biduality isomorphisms.

The finite field $A$ is a commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra by the given unital map. Apply the coefficient-change theorem to the bounded constructible dualizing input $K$ from Step 1. Its finite-field clause gives bounded constructibility of $K_A=A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K$ and preservation of all of $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ by $D_A=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,K_A)$, with natural evaluation-transpose biduality isomorphisms. In this case the theorem's finite-Tor category is the whole bounded constructible category.

The theorem in Step 2 supplies the evaluation-transpose map $M\to D_AD_AM$ for every $A$-complex $M$ in the stated category, not just an unspecified objectwise isomorphism. For a scalar-extended input $M=A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}N$, its comparison with the original biduality is the scalar-extension comparison in the cited statement. For a general $M$ no presentation as a scalar-extended object is asserted or needed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definition 7.1.1, Theorem 7.1.3, and the internal-Hom comparison of Theorem 7.6.1

proof.text: Use the residue-field pinnings of [def-per-potential-dualizing]. The field $A$ is finite free as a $\Lambda$-module, so after choosing a basis, forgetting coefficients identifies $A_X\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}(-)$ with a finite direct sum of copies of the identity. Restriction, the supported kernel defining $i^!$, and their right derived functors commute with these finite sums. This also computes the costalk over $A$: restriction of an injective $A$-sheaf is injective over $\Lambda$, since its Hom functor is the composite with the exact left adjoint $A_X\otimes_{\Lambda_X}(-)$. Consequently the canonical $A$-linear comparison is $R\Gamma_xK_A\simeq A\otimes_\Lambda R\Gamma_xK$. Tensoring $p_x$ gives $p_x^A:R\Gamma_xK_A\xrightarrow{\sim} A(\delta(x))[2\delta(x)]$, where $A(d)=A\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda(d)$. These maps retain the residue-field Galois action; their compatibility is checked on geometric fibres in the next step.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definitions 1.1.1, 1.4.1 and 2.1.2; finite-free scalar extension of the supported-kernel construction

proof.text: For an immediate geometric specialization $\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar x$, start with the current defining equality $p_{\bar y}=p_{\bar x}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar x}$. The transition recipe in [def-per-potential-dualizing] commutes with the finite direct sums of Step 4: restriction and supported kernels do so; on the normalized trait, averaging, evaluation at a generator, and inverse evaluation at $1-\sigma$ are additive $\Lambda$-linear operations. Tensoring their maps and inverse maps thus gives the same recipe over $A$. The degree $d=[\kappa(\widetilde z_0):\kappa(z_0)]$ is the one after strict localization; its inverse maps to the inverse in $A$. Hence $\operatorname{sp}^A=1_A\otimes\operatorname{sp}$, and tensoring the defining equality gives $p^A_{\bar y}=p^A_{\bar x}(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}^A_{\bar y,\bar x}$ in $D^+(A)$. Roots-of-unity transport and $\delta(y)=\delta(x)+1$ identify the targets. This verifies the claimed normalization with the corrected geometric-fibre equation. Neither duality theorem introduces a residue-field cohomological-dimension hypothesis.

I also read every cited node statement, the citer lem-per-finite-residue-dualizing and the ancestor lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve, which has no blueprint_update. The item statement is unchanged. Earlier faults: (1) is repaired. lem-per-gabber-local-duality-general is now Z/ℓ^r with ℓ invertible, cites the existing prime-power def-per-potential-dualizing-complex and def-exc-excellent-ring, and matches 6.1.1 hypothesis by hypothesis. (2a) is repaired. Constructibility with finitely generated stalks and finite Tor amplitude for general Noetherian A are defined inline; def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude covers only O_E/ϖ^n on the pro-étale site. (2b), ℓ invertible, was not a real fault: ILO §7 and Lemma 6.2.2.4 assume only 'X noethérien', and the proof of 7.1.3 never uses invertibility. (2c) is repaired: the 7.6.1 scalar-extension clause is limited to inputs A⊗N, where ctf = c over F_ℓ. Steps: Step 1 is correct; at r=1 the two potential-complex definitions encode the same ILO Def 2.1.2 (μ_ℓ twist, geometric-fibre pinnings, strict-local immediacy, normalized trait transition divided by the residue degree after strict localization). Step 2 uses the finite-field clause and gives the item's first three clauses. Step 3 is redundant but harmless. Step 4 is elementary: A is finite free over Λ, injective A-sheaves restrict to injective Λ-sheaves, so RΓ_x K_A ≅ A⊗RΓ_x K. Step 5 is elementary: every piece of the sp recipe is additive, so sp^A = 1⊗sp and the geometric-fibre equation survives tensoring. Small cases checked: X empty, a separably closed point, Spec F_q, A = Λ, A = F_{ℓ^2}, A = F_ℓ[t] in the coefficient node, a purely inseparable trait. Duplicate grep (6.1.1, 7.1.3, 7.6.1, biduality with dualizing): the NK prime-power uniqueness node has no biduality, and the finite-field-datum six-functor nodes are only over F̄_q, so there is no duplicate.
